$comment: The CROSS-LANGUAGE conformance vector for AuthorizeRequest.tool_input_digest.
Contract: canonicalize the tool input as RFC 8785 (JCS) JSON, then
Every SDK and framework adapter MUST reproduce `canonical` byte-for-byte and `digest`
character-for-character from `input`. The Rust reference is
crates/seam-api/tests/authorize_jcs_digest_vector.rs. There is deliberately NO bless mode: a
mismatch is a CONTRACT BREAK, not a prompt to regenerate. The digest is a one-way door — it is
what call_sig signs and what the advisory audit row records.
`input` is written here in ordinary JSON; a conformant implementation canonicalizes IT, not the

cases.name: empty-object
cases.why: the degenerate input every adapter hits first (a no-argument tool)

cases.name: key-ordering
cases.why: JCS sorts object keys by UTF-16 code unit; an insertion-ordered serializer diverges here

cases.name: nested-and-arrays
cases.why: array order is significant (never sorted) while nested object keys are sorted

cases.name: numbers
cases.why: JCS numbers are ECMAScript Number::toString — integral doubles lose their .0, and exponents normalize

cases.name: strings-and-escapes
cases.why: JCS escapes only what JSON requires; everything else is literal UTF-8 (no \uXXXX for non-ASCII)

input.text:
quote" backslash\ tab	 newline
 emoji😀 accents éü

cases.canonical: {"text":"quote\" backslash\\ tab\t newline\n emoji😀 accents éü"}

cases.name: unicode-key-ordering
cases.why: JCS orders keys by UTF-16 code units, which differs from UTF-8 byte order above U+FFFF

cases.name: literals
cases.why: true/false/null render bare, and a top-level array is a legal input too
